metadata.title: Jovenes en Orbita | Explore the Cosmos
metadata.description: Discover the mysteries of the universe: from the composition of dark matter to constellations.

hero.subtitle: Explore the mysteries of the cosmos, from the smallest particles to the largest structures in the universe.

universe.title: The Universe 13.8 billion
universe.subtitle: How did everything that exists come to be?
universe.description: The Big Bang is the most widely accepted cosmological theory about the origin of the universe. Approximately 13.8 billion years ago, all matter, energy, space, and time began to expand from an extremely dense and hot state, giving rise to everything we know.

matter.title: What is the Universe made of?
matter.darkEnergyDesc: A mysterious form of energy that makes up approximately 68% of the universe and is responsible for the accelerated expansion of the cosmos.
matter.darkMatterDesc: Invisible matter that neither emits nor absorbs light. It makes up 27% of the universe and its presence is detected by its gravitational effects.
matter.antimatterDesc: Matter composed of antiparticles, which have the same mass but opposite charge to normal particles. Its contact with matter produces annihilation.
matter.baryonicDesc: The ordinary matter that makes up everything visible: stars, planets, and ourselves. It represents only 5% of the universe.
matter.lightDesc: Visible electromagnetic radiation that travels at 299,792 km/s. It is our main tool for observing and understanding the universe.
matter.darkEnergyFullDesc: Dark energy is a form of energy that fills all of space and tends to accelerate the expansion of the universe. It is the greatest mystery of modern cosmology.
matter.darkMatterFullDesc: Dark matter does not emit light and cannot be seen directly, but we know it is there by the gravitational pull it exerts on galaxies.
matter.antimatterFullDesc: Antimatter is the opposite of matter. When a particle of matter meets its antiparticle, they annihilate each other, releasing pure energy.
matter.baryonicFullDesc: Baryonic matter is everything we can see and touch. It is made of atoms, which in turn are made of protons, neutrons, and electrons.
matter.lightFullDesc: Light is both a particle and a wave. It is the messenger of the universe, allowing us to see galaxies that existed billions of years ago.

planets.title: Solar System
planets.subtitle: Our cosmic neighborhood: eight unique planets orbiting our star, the Sun.
planets.mercuryShortDesc: The smallest and closest planet to the Sun. A rocky world without an atmosphere and extreme temperatures.
planets.venusShortDesc: Often called Earth's twin due to its similar size, but with a thick, toxic atmosphere that makes it the hottest.
planets.earthShortDesc: Our home, the only known planet to harbor life and have liquid water on its surface.
planets.marsShortDesc: The red planet. A cold, desert world with a very thin atmosphere, home to the largest volcano in the solar system.
planets.jupiterShortDesc: The gas giant, the largest planet in our system. It has a Great Red Spot that is a giant storm.
planets.saturnShortDesc: Famous for its stunning ring system. A gas giant composed mainly of hydrogen and helium.
planets.uranusShortDesc: An ice giant that orbits on its side. Its blue-green color comes from methane in its atmosphere.
planets.neptuneShortDesc: The most distant and windiest planet. A dark, cold world whipped by supersonic winds.

moonSection.title: The 5 Largest Moons in the Solar System
moonSection.subtitle: Fascinating natural satellites orbiting the gas giants and our own planet.
moonSection.ganymedeHistory: Ganymede is the largest moon in the Solar System and the only one with its own magnetic field. It orbits Jupiter and is even larger than the planet Mercury.
moonSection.titanHistory: Titan is Saturn's largest moon and the only one with a dense atmosphere. It has lakes of liquid methane and ethane, making it a fascinating place for science.
moonSection.callistoHistory: Callisto is Jupiter's second largest moon. Its surface is the oldest and most cratered in the Solar System, with almost no geological activity.
moonSection.ioHistory: Io is the most volcanically active body in the Solar System. It orbits so close to Jupiter that tidal forces constantly heat its interior.
moonSection.theMoonHistory: Our Moon is the fifth largest satellite and the only place outside Earth where humans have set foot. It vitally influences Earth's tides.

constellationSection.title: Constellations
constellationSection.description: In order to easily identify the seasons and recognize both the movements and positions of celestial bodies observed in the sky, ancient astronomers created drawings based on human, animal, and object shapes, formed by connecting nearby stars in the sky; these were named constellations.

astronomicalFact.imageCaption: Image of Earth captured from 6 billion kilometers away
astronomicalFact.description: Human beings are very curious; it is part of our nature, and to a large extent this curiosity has brought us to where we are today. Scientists around the world work hard to understand the phenomena that surround us in the Universe, and that is why new advances and notable discoveries in the field of astronomy constantly emerge.

gallery.title: Astronomical Photo Gallery
gallery.description: Major space agencies such as NASA and ESA, with the support of hundreds and even thousands of people and institutions around the world, have managed to create enormous and powerful telescopes, with "James Webb" currently being the most powerful ever created. They amaze us with spectacular high-resolution images of various structures present in the cosmos.

footer.aboutText1: The "Jovenes en Orbita" website was designed to teach the public about science, specifically in the area of knowledge about the cosmos, its composition, origin, and structures present in it. Here, you will find vital information about a wide variety of celestial bodies, from their origin, evolution, and end of their existence, to phenomena present both in our daily lives and billions of light-years away.
footer.aboutText2: The website was created to be an entertaining way to learn about the nature of everything that existed, exists, and will exist. It also provides several sources of information if you are interested in learning in person about this field of science.
footer.weeklyNote: The astronomical fact will be updated every week with new and varied information.

structuresPage.metaDescription: Discover the main structures of the cosmos: from galaxy superclusters to comets and meteoroids.
structuresPage.title: Structures in the Universe
structuresPage.subtitle: The universe contains an amazing variety of structures, from the largest such as galaxy superclusters, to the smallest such as meteoroids. Explore each one of them.

superclusters.title: Superclusters
superclusters.description: Superclusters are one of the largest structures in the universe. They are large groupings of galaxy clusters formed by hundreds of galaxies that interact gravitationally, spanning millions of light-years.

galaxyClusters.title: Galaxy Clusters
galaxyClusters.description: Groupings of tens, or even hundreds of galaxies that interact gravitationally with each other. Also composed of large clouds of hot gas, although most of their mass is dark matter.

galaxies.title: Galaxies
galaxies.description: Galaxies are the largest collections of stars in the universe. In one, hundreds of millions of stars are bound together by gravitational attraction.

nebulae.title: Nebulae
nebulae.description: Nebulae are large accumulations of gas and dust scattered throughout practically all of interstellar space.

starClusters.title: Star Clusters
starClusters.description: Star clusters are gigantic groupings of stars attracted to each other by their mutual gravitational pull.

stars.title: Stars
stars.description: Stars are enormous spheres of gas that use various chemical elements to release energy and heat through nuclear reactions.

neutronStars.title: Neutron Stars
neutronStars.description: Neutron stars are stellar remnants that have reached the end of their evolutionary journey through space and time.

blackHoles.title: Black Holes
blackHoles.description: Black holes are the cold remnants of ancient stars, so dense that no material particle, not even light, can escape their powerful gravitational pull.

planetarySystems.title: Planetary Systems
planetarySystems.description: Planetary systems are collections of celestial bodies, formed by one or more central stars and smaller bodies that orbit around them due to gravity.

planets.title: Planets
planets.description: Planets are bodies that commonly orbit a star, have a spherical shape, and reflect light.

asteroids.title: Asteroids
asteroids.description: Asteroids are primarily irregularly shaped rocky masses or interplanetary debris, ranging from a few meters to hundreds of kilometers in diameter.

comets.title: Comets
comets.description: Comets, like asteroids, are interplanetary debris. Rocky and icy remnants from the formation of the Solar System.

meteoroids.title: Meteoroids, Meteorites, and Meteors
meteoroids.description: What is the difference between these similar and frequently confused concepts today?

datoPage.metaDescription: Facts, curiosities, and astronomical discoveries of the last century.
datoPage.title: Astronomical facts and discoveries of the last century
datoPage.intro: Human beings are very curious; it is part of our nature, and to a large extent this curiosity has brought us to where we are today. Be that as it may, here we have some answers to the big questions...
datoPage.articleTitle: A hundred exoplanets float freely in the Milky Way
datoPage.articleSubtitle: Scientists from the Center for Astrobiology (CSIC-INTA) have observed that in one of the nearest star-forming regions, Upper Scorpius, one of the largest populations of rogue planets discovered to date can be found. They do not orbit stars, but instead wander through that area of the Milky Way.
datoPage.articleImageAlt: Pale Blue Dot - Earth seen from 6 billion km
datoPage.articleBody: The Universe can be a tremendously threatening place when we consider the fragility of our fragile and lonely blue world. Black holes, supernova explosions, gamma-ray bursts, asteroids, or our own star, the Sun, are just some of the threats that could wipe out the trace of our species in one fell swoop and forever. Each new discovery we make about the cosmos puts us in a better position to understand our place in it. Scientists around the world work hard to understand the phenomena that surround us in the Universe, and that is why here we show some of the most notable advances made in the field of astronomy.

universePage.title: The Universe
universePage.subtitle: A journey from the beginning of time to the vastness of today.
universePage.originContent: About 13.8 billion years ago, the universe began with the Big Bang. It wasn't an explosion in space, but an expansion of space itself. From an infinitesimally small and hot point, the cosmos has been expanding and cooling ever since.
universePage.evolutionContent: As the universe cooled, energy converted into matter. First simple atoms formed, then the first stars and galaxies. For billions of years, the universe has evolved into the vast network of structures we observe today.
universePage.compositionContent: Surprisingly, everything we can see —stars, planets, people— represents only 5% of the universe. The rest is dark matter (27%), which holds galaxies together, and dark energy (68%), which accelerates the expansion of the cosmos.
universePage.charDesc1: The observable universe has a diameter of about 93 billion light-years and contains trillions of galaxies.
universePage.charDesc2: Space itself is expanding in all directions, and it does so faster and faster due to dark energy.
universePage.charDesc3: The entire cosmos is governed by fundamental laws like gravity and electromagnetism, constant throughout space-time.

argentinaSpacePage.title: Argentina in Space
argentinaSpacePage.subtitle: A journey through the history, present, and future of Argentine aerospace development.
argentinaSpacePage.historyContent: Argentina has a long tradition in the space sector. From the first rocket launches in the 60s to the creation of CONAE in the 90s, the country has demonstrated exceptional technical capacity in the Southern Cone.
argentinaSpacePage.satellitesContent: Missions like SAC-D and the SAOCOM constellation have positioned Argentina as a leader in Earth observation with microwave radar technology.
argentinaSpacePage.launchersContent: The Tronador project seeks to provide Argentina with its own satellite launch vehicle, allowing complete sovereignty in access to space.
argentinaSpacePage.companiesContent: INVAP, VENG, and numerous technological startups form a robust industrial ecosystem that exports technology to the entire world.
argentinaSpacePage.futureContent: With the development of smaller satellites, lunar exploration in international collaboration, and the refinement of launchers, the future is bright.

skyPage.title: Observe the Sky
skyPage.subtitle: Practical guide to enjoying astronomy from anywhere.
skyPage.astrotourismContent: Argentina has some of the cleanest skies in the world. From San Juan to Patagonia, there are national parks dedicated to stargazing.
skyPage.mapsContent: Download our updated star maps to identify constellations, planets, and celestial events visible this month.
skyPage.photographyContent: Basic tips for capturing the Milky Way with your camera or smartphone. Using a tripod and long exposures is the key.
skyPage.tipsContent: Get away from light pollution, let your eyes get used to the darkness, and use red lights so as not to lose night adaptation.

about.title: Jovenes en Orbita
about.description: We are a platform dedicated to scientific and astronomical outreach, born with the mission of bringing the cosmos closer to new generations in an interactive and modern way.
about.missionContent: To inspire curiosity about the universe through cutting-edge educational technology and rigorous scientific content.
about.foundersContent: A multidisciplinary team of astronomers, developers, and educators passionate about space.
about.partnersContent: We collaborate with educational institutions and observatories to ensure the accuracy of our information.
about.quote: The universe is out there, waiting for you to discover it.
